artifacts.summary: Confirms the jq-whole-object-into-head-1-under-pipefail SIGPIPE root cause at literature-briefing.sh:238-241,245-247 with a live reproduction; validates and recommends the jq-internal first()/-c fix over the head-1 idiom; audits all 10 head -1 sites in the file (8 confirmed safe/scalar).

memory_candidates.content: Bash idiom bug class: `jq <query-that-can-emit-an-object-or-array> | head -N` under `set -o pipefail` can SIGPIPE (exit 141) when the pretty-printed JSON is large enough that head closes the pipe before jq finishes writing -- a pipe-buffer-size race, so it only fails on large payloads, not small ones (looks intermittent). Fix: either add `-c` to force single-line output so head -N reads exactly what jq wrote, or (preferred) bound the result inside jq itself with `first(EXPR)` or `limit(N; EXPR)` and drop `head` from the pipeline entirely -- this also avoids scanning the whole input after the first match, which the head-based idiom wastefully does. Verified: `first(...)`/`limit(1;...)` over an empty match still exits 0 with empty output under `set -e`, so no `|| true` guard is needed when replacing a `head -1` no-match fallback pattern.
